findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on the datetime key used by the audit log endpoint
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint instantiates this paginator with order_by='-datetime', so self.key is 'datetime'. Here get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, 'datetime'), which is a datetime object; both raise TypeError ('must be real number, not datetime'). build_cursor calls get_item_key on the first result even for the initial page, so every request with optimized_pagination=true made by a superuser or global-access member returns a 500. The class needs the strftime-based conversion used by DateTimePaginator.get_item_key (or the endpoint must not use this paginator for datetime ordering).

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a number for a datetime column, so subsequent pages filter incorrectly or fail
findings.body: value_from_cursor returns cursor.value verbatim, an int/float. BasePaginator.build_queryset appends this value as the SQL parameter for the range predicate on the sort column, so against the audit log's timestamp column it will issue something like 'WHERE ...datetime <= <integer>'. PostgreSQL has no implicit cast from integer to timestamptz, so this produces a DB error or wrong comparisons on page 2 and beyond even after the get_item_key TypeError is fixed. DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor converts the cursor value back into a datetime; this paginator must do the same.

findings.title: Advanced negative-offset branch passes negative indices to a Django QuerySet, which raises ValueError
findings.body: The comment states the underlying Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically', but QuerySet.__getitem__ raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.') whenever the start index is negative. Cursor offsets are user-controlled via Cursor.from_string, so a crafted cursor with offset < 0 combined with optimized_pagination=true reaches this branch and produces a 500 rather than enabling reverse pagination. Negative offsets must be rejected (4xx) or clamped; passing them straight to a QuerySet cannot be a performance optimization.

findings.title: Negative offset guard in BasePaginator only applies to non-prev cursors
findings.body: start_offset is clamped with max(0, offset) only when cursor.is_prev is false; when is_prev is true the raw cursor offset is used unchanged. Because Cursor.from_string parses negative integers, a request with a cursor such as '0:-5:1' still reaches queryset[<negative>:stop], and Django raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), returning a 500. The new comment claims negative offsets are safe, but the previous-page path remains unguarded.

findings.title: New comment claims negative offsets are allowed, but the change is comment-only
findings.body: The diff only adds comments above `self.offset = int(offset)`. That line already accepted negative integers before this PR, and Cursor.from_string already parses them, so nothing about offset handling changed. The comment is misleading and implies guards/validation that do not exist, which is especially dangerous because negative offsets actually cause Django to raise ValueError in the paginator slicing paths.

findings.title: No tests for the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds a ~100-line paginator class and a new request-controlled branch in OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, but no tests. Basic tests exercising the optimized path against the real order_by='-datetime' queryset, or a cursor with a negative offset, would have caught both the datetime TypeError and the negative-slicing ValueError. Add tests for the optimized endpoint branch, cursor round-tripping, and negative/prev cursor handling.
